project_name: Relay: AI Agent Job Orchestration Platform
descriptor: A distributed job-orchestration system for batch enrichment pipelines, ensuring reliability engineering at scale.

requirements.statement: The system must use Redis Streams or SQS for the durable job queue.
The system must ensure idempotent job processing to prevent double-processing of re-delivered jobs.
The system must implement a circuit breaker in front of every external API call with a documented fallback or fail-fast path.
The system must have a dead-letter queue for jobs that exhaust retries, with a triage runbook.
The system must provide structured JSON logging with correlation IDs threaded through queue, worker, and external call.
The system must display a live SLO dashboard with a real error budget, showing metrics like job success rate and p95 job latency.
The system must support multiple autoscaling worker processes.
The system must have a documented chaos-engineering drill to test system resilience.
The system must be deployed to a real production host.
The system must route low-confidence classifications to a review queue instead of the dead-letter queue.
The system must log low-confidence classifications with their correlation ID for traceability.
The system must validate output against a declared JSON schema before persisting it.
The system must provide a plain-language status view for RevOps and research-ops analysts.
The system must track job success rate, p95 job latency, DLQ rate, circuit breaker trip frequency, and queue depth over time.
The system must codify classified failure modes into the retry policy to automate DLQ triage.
The system must ensure that summaries are grounded strictly in the source data pulled for each item.
The system must ensure that classification runs against a fixed, pre-defined taxonomy for the domain.
The system must provide an SLO dashboard as the ongoing check for system performance.

stories.title: Process a job with idempotency and logging
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to process jobs idempotently, so that re-delivered jobs do not double-process.
acceptance: Given a job in the queue, When it is processed, Then it is logged with a correlation ID
Given a re-delivered job, When it is processed, Then it does not double-process
Trust: All job processing is logged with correlation IDs
stories.task_guidance: Implement job processing logic with idempotency checks and structured logging.

stories.title: Process jobs with durable queue and logging
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to process jobs using a durable queue, so that job processing is reliable and traceable.
acceptance: Given a job is submitted, When it is processed, Then it is logged with its correlation ID
Given a job is processed, When it is low-confidence, Then it is logged with its correlation ID
Trust: Given a job is processed, Then its processing is logged for traceability
stories.task_guidance: Use the existing job queue to process jobs and ensure logging includes correlation IDs for traceability.

stories.title: Handle API calls with circuit breaker and validation
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to handle API calls with a circuit breaker, so that I can prevent cascading failures and ensure data integrity.
acceptance: Given an API call is made, When the circuit breaker is closed, Then the call proceeds
Given an API call is made, When the circuit breaker is open, Then the call is blocked
Trust: Given output is generated, Then it is validated against the JSON schema before persisting
stories.task_guidance: Integrate a circuit breaker pattern for API calls and validate outputs against the JSON schema before persisting.

stories.title: Implement dead-letter queue with triage runbook
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to use a dead-letter queue, so that failed jobs are managed and triaged.
acceptance: Given a job, When retries are exhausted, Then it is moved to the dead-letter queue
Given a dead-letter queue, When a job is triaged, Then it is logged with a reason
Trust: Dead-letter queue entries are logged with correlation IDs
failure_paths: Job does not move to DLQ
stories.task_guidance: Set up dead-letter queue and create triage runbook for failed jobs.

stories.title: Display live SLO dashboard
stories.narrative: As a user, I want to see a live SLO dashboard, so that I can monitor system performance.
acceptance: Given the system, When jobs are processed, Then SLO metrics are updated live
Given the SLO dashboard, When an error occurs, Then it is reflected in the error budget
Trust: SLO metrics are logged with correlation IDs
stories.task_guidance: Implement SLO dashboard with live metrics display.

stories.title: Implement autoscaling for worker processes
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to autoscale worker processes, so that job processing adapts to load.
acceptance: Given job load increases, When workers are needed, Then they are autoscaled
Given job load decreases, When workers are not needed, Then they are scaled down
Trust: Autoscaling events are logged with correlation IDs
stories.task_guidance: Configure autoscaling for worker processes based on job queue depth.

stories.title: Route low-confidence jobs to review queue
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to route low-confidence jobs to a review queue, so that they are not auto-resolved.
acceptance: Given a low-confidence job, When it is processed, Then it is routed to the review queue
Given a review queue, When a job is added, Then it is logged with a correlation ID
Trust: Low-confidence jobs are logged with correlation IDs
failure_paths: Job does not route to review queue
Review queue entry is not logged
stories.task_guidance: Implement routing logic for low-confidence jobs to review queue.

stories.title: Codify DLQ triage into retry policy
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to codify DLQ triage into the retry policy, so that manual review is minimized.
acceptance: Given a DLQ entry, When it is triaged, Then the retry policy is updated
Given the retry policy, When a job fails, Then it follows the updated policy
Trust: DLQ triage updates are logged with correlation IDs
stories.task_guidance: Analyze DLQ entries and update retry policy based on triage results.

stories.title: Conduct chaos-engineering drills
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to conduct chaos-engineering drills, so that system resilience is tested.
acceptance: Given a chaos drill, When a worker is killed mid-job, Then the system recovers without data loss
Given a queue backlog, When it is forced, Then the system processes jobs without duplicates
Trust: Chaos drill events are logged with correlation IDs
stories.task_guidance: Plan and execute chaos-engineering drills to test system resilience.

stories.title: Deploy with monitoring and status view
stories.narrative: As an operations team, I want to deploy the system with monitoring, so that I can track system health and provide status updates.
acceptance: Given the system is deployed, When it is running, Then job success rate and latency are tracked
Given the system is deployed, When a status request is made, Then a plain-language status view is provided
Trust: Given the system is running, Then monitoring data is logged for auditability
stories.task_guidance: Deploy the system to the production host and ensure monitoring tracks job success rate, latency, and provides a status view.

stories.title: Ensure classification runs against fixed taxonomy
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to ensure classification runs against a fixed taxonomy, so that results are consistent and reliable.
acceptance: Given a classification task, When it is executed, Then it uses the fixed taxonomy
Given a classification task, When the taxonomy is unavailable, Then the task fails gracefully
Trust: Given a classification task, Then its execution is logged with the taxonomy version
stories.task_guidance: Ensure classification tasks reference the fixed taxonomy and log the taxonomy version used.

stories.title: Generate summaries grounded in source data
stories.narrative: As a system, I want to generate summaries grounded in source data, so that they are accurate and verifiable.
acceptance: Given a summary is generated, When source data is available, Then it is grounded in that data
Given a summary is generated, When source data is missing, Then the summary generation fails
Trust: Given a summary is generated, Then its source data is logged for verification
stories.task_guidance: Ensure summaries are generated using the source data and log the data used for verification.
